details.contract:
New argument: range: { type: "array", items: { type: "integer" } } — exactly two integers, [from, to], 1-based inclusive, meaningful only with what=source.

Behaviour: clamp to the resolved node's own extent [startLine, endLine]; never throw for an out-of-extent or inverted range. from is clamped into [startLine, endLine]; to is clamped into [from, endLine]. The payload keeps a single effective window (the existing SourcePayload.window), and why names the clamp when it happened — for example "range clamped to the node's extent 12-40" — so the caller sees that the request was narrowed instead of silently answered.

New what value: "outline". Payload: { target, what: "outline", why, path, members: [{ qn, kind, lines: [start, end], signature }] } built from reader.members(node.id) for a class-like node and reader.nodesByFile(node.fileId) for a file node, in source order. No new reader method, no new query.

If argument parsing does not already coerce array items to integers, extend src/shared/cli/args.ts for the declared items type inside this task; the manifest table stays the source of truth.
Do not change the window semantics for a plain what=source call, and do not touch source_drift.

details.contract:
Issue #11, parse half. Today src/shared/domain/diff.ts:162 passes --no-renames and parseNameStatus returns null for an R/C pair, which degrades the whole change set to the hash comparison.

Changes, all in src/shared/domain/diff.ts:
1. Drop --no-renames from the git invocation.
2. parseNameStatus parses R and C records (status, old path, new path) and SKIPS a malformed individual record instead of returning null for the whole output. Returning null stays reserved for a git failure, so one odd line can no longer empty the change set.
3. ChangeSet gains, additively:
     readonly entries: readonly ChangeEntry[];
   with
     export type ChangeState = "modified" | "added" | "deleted" | "renamed";
     export interface ChangeEntry { readonly state: ChangeState; readonly path: string; readonly from?: string; }
   A rename is ONE entry: {state: "renamed", path: <new path>, from: <old path>}. A copy is "added". Status letters map M/T -> modified, A -> added, D -> deleted, R -> renamed.
4. Keep `changed`, `removed`, `unmatched`, `degraded`, `degradedReason` exactly as they are, so no consumer breaks. `changed` contains the destination path of a rename and does not double-count it. Entries are sorted by path and every path goes through the existing containment check; a path outside repoRoot is dropped from entries and counted nowhere.

This task changes no payload: summary and impact keep rendering from `changed`/`removed` until the following task switches them to `entries`.
